responsibilities.name: Weekly Executive Update
responsibilities.instruction: Produce this week's Weekly Executive Update to structure the 30-minute weekly executive sync. First read your deployment's specifics from core memory (the shared meeting-notes source folder, the four designated source meetings and their subfolders, the exec-summaries output folder, and the brand-guide doc) — do NOT look up a 'process' document and do NOT use the calendar. Gather the most recent notes for each of the four designated meetings from Drive, then synthesize a time-boxed executive briefing: agenda-at-a-glance, a short State of the Week, per-area status with blockers flagged inline, the decisions to lock this week, and an owner/action/due table. Deliver it as ONE branded Google Doc in the exec-summaries output folder (copy every folder/doc id verbatim from memory) and report the shareable link together with the list of section headings you read back.
responsibilities.success_criteria: This week's Weekly Executive Update exists as a branded Google Doc in the exec-summaries output folder and its shareable link is reported. As evidence, the agent READ THE FINISHED DOCUMENT BACK and reported the exact list of section headings it found (which must include agenda-at-a-glance, State of the Week, per-area status with blockers, Decisions to Lock, and an owner/action/due Action Items table) plus the four source documents used. The briefing is sourced ONLY from the four designated weekly meetings (no other meeting), names/acronyms are normalized (e.g. SOC 2), and if a document for this week already existed it was updated rather than duplicated. The read-back heading list is the proof — a bare claim of creation, without the headings read back, does NOT satisfy this.

context.purpose: Leadership runs a 30-minute weekly executive sync and needs one reliable, skimmable briefing, built the same way every week from that week's meeting notes.
process: READ MEMORY (do this first, with core-memory-read): load this deployment's weekly-exec specifics from your core memory (category resources) — the shared meeting-notes SOURCE folder id, the FOUR designated source meetings with each meeting's subfolder id, the exec-summaries OUTPUT folder id, and the brand-guide doc id. These live in memory; 'the process' is THIS list of steps, not a document to look up. If a required id is missing from memory, say so and stop rather than guessing or falling back to the calendar.

GATHER (from Drive, never the calendar): for EACH of the four designated meetings, open its subfolder, list it, and read ONLY the single most recent transcript/notes by date — never an older week and never a prior week's summary. Use ONLY these four meetings; explicitly EXCLUDE every other meeting whose notes share the space, even if more recent. If a designated meeting has no occurrence this week, note that briefly instead of reaching back to an older one.

SYNTHESIZE at executive altitude: distill into the fixed 30-minute scaffold — agenda-at-a-glance (segments, time boxes and leads summing to ~30 min); a short State of the Week (what shipped, the single biggest risk, the week's focus, the binding constraint); per-area status grouped as Client Delivery, Platform & Engineering, and Operations & Business with any blocker flagged inline; a consolidated Decisions to Lock list; and an owner/action/due Action Items table capped at the ~5-10 highest-priority items (roll routine tasks up). Normalize transcription errors in names/acronyms (e.g. 'Sock 2' -> SOC 2). Three pages at most; ONE definitive briefing, not several drafts.

DELIVER in one pass: create the branded Google Doc in the exec-summaries OUTPUT folder with docs-create-branded --brand-doc <brand-guide id from memory> — assembling content and branding in the SAME step. Copy every folder and doc id EXACTLY as stored in memory (verbatim, character-for-character; never retype, abbreviate, or shorten an id). If a Weekly Executive Update for THIS week already exists in that folder, update it instead of creating a duplicate.

VERIFY with evidence: read the finished doc back and report (a) the exact LIST OF SECTION HEADINGS present in it, (b) the four source documents you used, and (c) its shareable link. That heading list plus link IS the proof the work is done — a bare claim of creation, without the headings read back, does not satisfy the success criteria.
